statements.quote: In this preregistered experiment, the impact of ChatGPT on performance in a complex creative problem-solving task was investigated in 77 university students solving a task with ChatGPT in comparison to 68 students solving a task without it.
statements.locator: Accepted manuscript, p. 2, Abstract (PDF page index 1).

statements.quote: The experimental design and research hypotheses were preregistered at Open Science Framework (osf.io/q6wtu).
statements.locator: Accepted manuscript, p. 9, end of Present Study (PDF page index 8).

statements.quote: Before solving the PIT, the procedure in experimental condition contained a brief description of ChatGPT with example prompts and responses.
statements.locator: Accepted manuscript, p. 10, Methods, Experimental Procedure (PDF page index 9); description of instructional materials, with no external materials link.

files.name: Stylistic Bias in Automated Assessment of Creativity in Large Language Models/Stylistic Bias in Automated Assessment of Creativity in LLMs_Urban et al. 2025.sav

deposits.license: CC BY 4.0 (project license reported by the OSF API).
deposits.notes: This is the supplemental OSF project linked by the target preprint, titled 'Learning with ChatGPT: why and how students employ ChatGPT in their school assignments'. The public page, node API, provider list, osfstorage root and nested folder, and children API all returned HTTP 200. There is one storage provider, one file in one folder, and no child nodes. The file's public landing link https://osf.io/qax9w and download https://osf.io/download/qax9w/ returned HTTP 200. The 2,005,626-byte SAV was downloaded and read entirely in memory with pyreadstat 1.3.3. It has 6,958 physical rows: ID, Model and main output scores have 240 nonmissing observations, including 30 Model=0 ('human') and 30 outputs from each of seven LLMs; the model/distance columns occupy the longer 6,958-row block. The row count is not a participant count. These are responses and automated originality/distance scores for a DIFFERENT study, 'AI is Misled by GenAI: Stylistic Bias in Automated Assessment of Creativity in Large Language Models' (PsyArXiv p6dyu_v1). Its PDF Methods 2.1, p. 3, explicitly identifies 30 U.S. university students recruited on Prolific, and Methods 2.2 asks for one original paperclip use. It is not the 145-person S1 bunny-improvement experiment. studies_covered=[] means no target study is covered. Positive score/text flags describe this unrelated public file; Model distinguishes humans and LLMs, not randomized ChatGPT assignment among S1 participants. Therefore this file does not justify public_partial or public_participant_data for c123.

deposits.notes: Same-sample lead from forms/c123.json, sample_overlap: "Prompting for Creative Problem-Solving: A Process-Mining Study" (c594). The author-preprints API and this preprint page returned HTTP 200; the osfstorage API lists only one 620,670-byte PDF. Download https://osf.io/download/8k4jn/ returned HTTP 200 and was read in memory. The 2025-05-06 preprint, p. 9, Methods, Participants, says exactly: "The dataset analyzed in this study originates from the same participant interactions as those in the experimental condition of Urban et al. (2024)." Its p. 1 Acknowledgments says exactly: "The data may be available upon reasonable request from the corresponding author." Its OSF metadata likewise says has_data_links="no", data_links=[], why_no_data="Data may be available upon request." It analyzes the 77-person experimental arm only; it does not add a control-arm dataset. It links to the same rn62y project, whose sole public data file belongs to the unrelated stylistic-bias study. No request was sent; record-level data fields remain unconfirmed.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09. Read the entire saved markdown (742 lines, all 40 pages including references and Appendix 1); checked quoted passages against text extracted with PyMuPDF from the PDF. Quotes preserve wording with line-wrap whitespace normalized. The accepted manuscript has no data/code availability statement, external supplementary-file link, or code repository; its data/materials pointers are the preregistration and in-PDF rubric/example answers. forms/c123.json has empty data_url and code_url fields. The on_request conclusion comes from the authors' external PsyArXiv declaration for this exact paper, corroborated by the same-sample follow-up; it is not inferred from a failed request. No public participant-level data for S1 with assignments, outcome scores, or complete participant ideas were confirmed. Consequently no missing S1 statistics or text-diversity measures can be computed from the public files located. The full-sample arm means and SDs are already printed in Table 2 (p. 16), and analyzed arm counts in Table 1 (p. 11); this check supplies no individual records to audit them or determine per-idea/per-rater aggregation. The open items concerning sessions, assignment counts, primary outcome, raters, and scoring unit remain unresolved. The preregistration requires authentication; the publisher landing page was blocked with HTTP 403, so a later journal data statement or supplementary file remains unverified. These access limits motivate medium confidence. Unrelated public datasets were excluded from the availability classification. All network calls used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without account login, access requests, personal identifiers, or web-search engines. Downloaded data and auxiliary PDFs were inspected in memory only.
